desk.headline: Sales up 11% to $5.18bn, beat; adjusted EPS $12.54 beat; 2026 sales and EPS outlook raised to $47–48
results: Sales rose 11.3% to $5.18bn, or 14.9% on an organic constant-currency basis after the UK exit; adjusted EPS jumped 23% to $12.54.
High-Touch Solutions (North America) grew 13.8% on double-digit volumes and price rises; Endless Assortment (Zoro and MonotaRO) grew 19.3% organically.
Gross margin edged up to 38.8%, though High-Touch slipped to 40.8% on freight and mix; adjusted operating margin rose to 16.1%.
Operating cash flow was $661m and free cash flow $546m; $396m went back to shareholders through dividends and buybacks.

guidance.summary: Grainger lifted its 2026 outlook again: sales of $19.8–20.0bn and adjusted EPS of $47.00–48.00, both above the August ranges. On the call it pointed to Q4 sales above $4.9bn.

points: Demand kept strengthening through the year, helped largely by data-centre and power projects; October sales grew about 18%.
Grainger raised prices about 1% in September, mostly due to costs tied to the Middle East conflict, and is weighing more from 1 January.
Higher diesel costs hurt freight margins; a tariff refund was largely offset by a fire-related inventory write-off in Louisville.
For Q4, management pointed to sales above $4.9bn and an operating margin near 15.5%, with seasonal costs and higher bonuses.
The CEO called the reset of incentive pay a meaningful tailwind for 2027; the August technology acquisition is a small margin drag.
call.source: Call summary — GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance, 4 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether customers accept further price increases planned for January.
Q4 margin, with seasonal costs, higher bonuses and acquisition integration.
Data-centre-driven project demand and Zoro's growth into 2027.
